findings.quote: at times people even bridge it for those who wish to cross on foot between the continents, and at all times it is traversed by shipping
findings.problem: Greek has ποτὲ μὲν γεφυρούμενον ... ποτὲ δὲ πλωτευόμενον συνεχῶς: at times bridged, at other times sailed across continuously. The μὲν...δέ contrast is lost; 'at all times' is not in the Greek.
findings.proposed_fix: at times it is bridged by those who choose to cross on foot to either continent, and at other times it is continuously crossed by ships

units.note: Minor; remainder of chapter accurate (60 stades vs 2 stades correct).

findings.quote: and shattered the sarissas of others, then with the broken splinters stabbed their faces and exposed parts, throwing them into total confusion.
findings.problem: Greek has a lacuna: ὧν δὲ συντρίβοντες τὰς σαρίσας αὐτοῖς τοῖς ἐκείνων κλάσμασιν ἐκ διαλήψεως *** τύπτοντες αὐτῶν ταῖς ἐπιδορατίσι τὰ πρόσωπα. The text breaks off after ἐκ διαλήψεως, and the English reads on as if whole. It also omits ταῖς ἐπιδορατίσι (spear-points/butt-spikes) and the force of ἐκ διαλήψεως.
findings.proposed_fix: and breaking the sarissas of others, with the very fragments of them, [gap in the Greek text] striking their faces and exposed parts with the spear-points, they drove them into complete rout.

units.note: Lacuna marked with a bracketed gap; no text invented. Meaning of ἐκ διαλήψεως in context is uncertain because of the gap.
Greek breaks off at εἰσπο- and resumes in ch. 37 (ρεύεσθαι); English joins the sentence correctly.
